☕ THE LEAD

Well, if you thought the Jensen Huang saga was over, think again. Nvidia’s co-founder and CEO, who resigned less than two weeks ago amidst allegations of affairs and sharing intel with China, is officially back at the helm. And get this: President Trump reportedly called into the board meeting to advocate for his return, saying he "convinced them" and that the U.S. has no evidence of wrongdoing [S2][S14][S46][S60][S63][S65][S66]. Huang was greeted by cheering employees, promising to be a "better CEO the second time around" [S43][S45]. But not everyone's thrilled – politicians are calling it "outrageous" and "reckless," and he's slated to testify in the Senate next week [S48][S54]. The underlying drama here isn't just about a CEO; it's about the immense power of Nvidia in the AI world, the political stakes involved, and how quickly public perception (and board decisions) can pivot when market value is on the line [S55][S59]. The takeaway? In the current AI gold rush, some players are simply too big to fail—or stay away.

📣 QUICK HITS

**Mailchimp sells for less than a third of its acquisition price.**
Intuit offloaded the email marketing platform to Bending Spoons for a fraction of the $12 billion it paid in 2021, a clear sign that the market is re-evaluating tech valuations, especially for legacy platforms that aren't *deeply* integrated into the AI wave [S12].

**Agencies are still selling AI efficiency, but clients want outcomes.**
Two years in, clients are tired of hearing about "faster work" and "leaner teams" if their invoices aren't shrinking and their business isn't growing. The real opportunity for agencies with AI isn't doing the same work cheaper, it's driving better results and growth [S11].

**A24 launches a "scent score" for its new horror film ‘Backrooms’.**
Brooklyn fragrance house Joya Studio collaborated with A24 to create five bespoke scents (like "Static" and "Wet") designed to be sprayed at specific timestamps while watching the movie. This is next-level experiential marketing, turning passive viewing into a multi-senssensory, immersive event [S17].

**Brands are boosting Black Friday spending, with shifts in tactics.**
Digiday Research shows marketers are adjusting holiday tactics in 2026, with media buyers projecting 10-30% more spend on digital media for Black Friday/Cyber Monday compared to last year. Retail media (especially Amazon), search, CTV, and YouTube are soaking up most of that increase [S27][S30].

🎯 THE PMM DESK

**Anthropic's Claude Ship introduces AI agents for code review.**
Claude now offers "PR Steward" and "Claude Approvals" agents, allowing the AI to review pull requests, fix failing CI checks, resolve merge conflicts, and even approve code on its own. For PMMs, this is a clear product expansion targeting developer workflow efficiency, requiring sharp messaging around trust, autonomy, and speed [S44].

**Nothing unveils Ear Note earbuds with AI transcription.**
Carl Pei's Nothing is launching the "Ear Note," earbuds with a microphone-equipped charging case that can record and transcribe conversations, generating AI summaries. This is a classic feature-driven product positioning play: the core value proposition revolves around hands-free AI notetaking, making the "how" (earbuds) secondary to the "what" (AI transcription) [S51].

🧠 PMM 101

**The concept:** Feature-Benefit-Value Framework
**What it is:** This framework helps you articulate what your product (or a specific feature) *does* (feature), what problem it *solves* for the user (benefit), and the ultimate impact or outcome it creates for their life or business (value). It moves beyond just listing specs.
**Why it matters:** Buyers don't buy features; they buy solutions and outcomes. This framework ensures your messaging resonates by focusing on what truly matters to them.
**See it today:** Nothing's Ear Note earbuds. The *feature* is AI transcription [S51]. The *benefit* is effortlessly capturing conversations and meetings without manual notes. The *value* is increased productivity, better recall, and less mental load, freeing up time and cognitive energy.
**Try it:** Pick a new feature from a product you love. Can you clearly state its feature, benefit, and value? Now, try it for a feature of your *own* product (or a hypothetical one). Practice moving from "it does X" to "so you can Y" to "which means Z for your goals."

🧩 PRODUCT CORNER

**Google Search's AI Mode now integrates with Drive and Wallet for personalized results.**
Google is deepening its "Personal Intelligence" in AI Mode by allowing it to tap into your Google Drive and Wallet data. This means more personalized search responses, leveraging the wealth of user data already within Google's ecosystem to make AI search more relevant and contextual [S50]. It's a significant move towards making AI assistants truly personal, but also raises interesting questions about data privacy and user trust.

🔧 TOOL DROP

**FigmaMCP** — Let Claude Code or Codex edit your open Figma file.
Best for: Designers and developers looking to automate design iterations or translate designs to code using AI. · Free tier: No · Honest take: Genuinely useful. This bridges the design-to-dev gap with AI, potentially saving tons of time on repetitive tasks and accelerating prototyping. Worth checking out if you're in a design-heavy role. [S10]

⚡ SPEED ROUND

⌚ Apple Watch Series 12 is hitting an all-time low of $299 for Black Friday, $100 off its usual price [S1].
🍺 Modelo is now the NCAA's first official beer, focusing on March Madness but covering over 90 championships [S19].
🔒 TikTok added new AI transparency and parental controls after its Safety and Innovation Summit [S37].
📉 Meta just scrapped its 2030 net-zero goal, a move that could anger competitors and environmental advocates [S58].
🍮 Jell-O is making its largest marketing investment in over a decade with a new creative platform focusing on shifting consumer perceptions [S22].
🚗 Uber rolled out "Recorded Rides," an option to book trips that record the entire drive using the driver's front camera [S67].
